item.description: THE ELON EFFECT: Terafab is already attracting more companies to Texas’ Brazos Valley. 🇺🇸 The Greater Brazos Partnership says other companies have started calling since Terafab was announced, hoping to join the region’s growth. Local leaders estimate Terafab will account for roughly 15% of the region’s total growth over the next decade. Texas A&M expects at least 50 students to begin its new master’s program in microelectronics and semiconductors this year. This is the Elon effect. Terafab will help America manufacture advanced AI chips at home for use on Earth and in space. As Greater Brazos Partnership CEO Tom Johnson said: “This is a winner.”

item.description: Starlink is taking over aviation. The number of airlines announcing deals with Starlink is surging, and the reason is simple: airlines without Starlink now risk losing passengers to competitors offering a much better onboard connectivity experience. We are already seeing evidence of this on 𝕏, with many passengers saying they are choosing one airline over another specifically because it offers Starlink.

item.description: Last week,@SpaceXAIreleased Grok 4.6, its new frontier model designed for coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work. Independent evaluations suggest that SpaceXAI has returned to the AI frontier competition based on both performance and cost. The economics of Grok 4.6 seem particularly compelling for AI agents. Artificial Analysis estimates that Grok 4.6 costs $0.84 per task on its Intelligence Index, placing it on the Pareto frontier for intelligence-versus-cost. item.title: @elonmusk: 🚨David Friedberg predicts the path to “Comrade AOC,” national asset seizures, and data centers becom...
item.description: 🚨David Friedberg predicts the path to “Comrade AOC,” national asset seizures, and data centers becoming the next target. “They enact policy starting in 2028 with Comrade AOC in charge… costs balloon, the bond market sells off… and now the 30-year yield spikes 7%, 8%, maybe more.” Higher rates make housing even less affordable. Then the government needs more money. “So now we need to pass a national asset seizure tax.” But there isn’t enough wealth at the top. “The total net worth of all people that are worth over $50 million is only $23 trillion.”@DavidSackspoints to a Cato estimate putting nine DSA-style proposals at $71 TRILLION to $212 TRILLION over 10 years. The entire Forbes 400 is worth just $6.6 trillion. Eventually, Friedberg argues, you run out of billionaires to tax and move toward confiscation and scapegoating.@chamath: “The billionaires will be scapegoated, and the trillionaires will be, I mean, even worse.” Then tech becomes the target: “The data center is the temple where the billionaires and trillionaires pray.”@friedberg’s warning: massive DSA-style government spending makes the affordability crisis worse, fuels resentment, and eventually creates the political justification for national asset seizures. Full episode:@theallinpod
